title: The Summit of the Upper Fly River
premise: August Iversen, a disgraced mountain guide hiding in the border town of Kessik, is dragged back into the high country when his old rival Soren Vask hires his crew to escort a mining magnate's daughter across the Upper Fly range before early snows seal the passes. The route crosses territory August swore off after an expedition that killed three climbers and buried his reputation, and he soon realizes Vask's real cargo is not the daughter but evidence that could destroy them both. Betrayed mid-range by a crew member reporting to the magnate, August must choose between saving himself and protecting the woman who has become his only witness. In the end, August reaches the far side with the truth intact, surrenders his anonymity to testify, and finds that survival was never about staying invisible—it was about deciding what was worth being seen for.
about_author: K. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent a decade outfitting climbs across remote northern ranges before turning to fiction. They write from a small cabin office, drawing on field journals and the stories guides tell when the radios are off.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgets on Purpose
chapters.summary: August Iversen's POV. August works low-stakes river runs in Kessik, keeping his name out of permit ledgers, until a letter arrives bearing a signature he hoped never to see again. The beat is uneasy quiet before a storm; we learn his blacklist and the accident that caused it.

chapters.title: A Signature Like a Knife
chapters.summary: August's POV. He burns the letter, but its terms—double pay, one crossing, no questions—haunt him through a sleepless night. His business partner Tomas urges refusal. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into curiosity, the old hunger for the high country stirring.

chapters.title: Soren Vask at the Door
chapters.summary: August's POV. Vask appears in person, older, richer, unapologetic about the past. He offers the job: escort Ilse Brandt, daughter of mining magnate Henrik Brandt, over the Upper Fly before the equinox snows. August refuses. Beat: two predators circling, old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Ilse Brandt's POV, first appearance. In her father's offices she discovers discrepancies in the mine's environmental filings and realizes her planned 'holiday trek' is also her father's way of moving her—and possibly a courier's satchel—out of reach of investigators. Beat: suspicion born.

chapters.title: The Crew Assembles
chapters.summary: August's POV. Money pressures force his hand; he signs on but sets conditions: his route, his rules. He recruits guide Mara Quist, cook Renny, and porter Dev Okafor—a stranger whose references are too clean. Beat: reluctant commitment, the crew as a fragile machine.

chapters.title: Ilse Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She meets August and recognizes him from the scandal files her father kept. She says nothing. Their first exchange is polite fencing, each measuring the other. Beat: mutual misreading—she thinks him mercenary, he thinks her spoiled.

chapters.title: Gear, Lies, and Weight Limits
chapters.summary: Mara Quist's POV. Packing day: Mara notices the manifest includes equipment no sightseeing client needs—satellite uplink cases, sealed drums—and quietly re-weighs everything. Beat: professional unease; the reader sees the cargo problem forming before August does.

chapters.title: The Lower Trail
chapters.summary: Dev Okafor's POV. First days on trail; Dev photographs gear and sends coded updates via a relay beacon, revealing he reports to someone inside Brandt Mining. Beat: dramatic irony—the reader now knows there's a traitor, and it isn't who August suspects.

chapters.title: River Crossing at Kettle Ford
chapters.summary: August's POV. A glacial ford nearly takes Renny's pack train; August's competence saves it, and Ilse watches him work with new eyes. First real conversation. Beat: grudging respect beginning to replace contempt on both sides.

chapters.title: Vask's Shadow
chapters.summary: Soren Vask's POV. Vask follows a parallel valley route with a second team, radioing Dev for position checks. We learn Vask's stake: he helped falsify the mine filings years ago and needs the original documents recovered or destroyed. Beat: villain interiority, motive clarified.

chapters.title: The Tree Line
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The crew enters the high forest; Ilse asks August directly about the disaster that blacklisted him. He gives a clipped, partial answer—three dead, his fault, case closed. Beat: intimacy attempted and deflected; weather turning.

chapters.title: First Snow, Wrong Season
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. An unseasonal dusting confirms the window is shrinking faster than forecast. Mara confronts August privately about the sealed drums; he opens one and finds survey cores and a ledger of falsified readings. Beat: the job's true shape revealed.

chapters.title: Terms Renegotiated at Altitude
chapters.summary: August's POV. August tells Ilse what he found. She admits she suspected and reveals her own goal: get the originals to regulators on the far side, beyond her father's lawyers. Uneasy alliance formed. Beat: purpose aligned, trust still provisional.

chapters.title: Dev's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Ordered to sabotage the satphone and delay the party until Vask intercepts, Dev hesitates—he has come to like the crew. He loosens a fuel line instead of cutting it, buying time. Beat: conscience flickering in a bought man.

chapters.title: The Col of Hanging Ice
chapters.summary: August's POV. A technical pitch under seracs; August leads, Ilse follows well, proving herself. A minor fall injures Renny's wrist. Beat: competence porn and rising stakes—the mountain itself becoming an antagonist.

chapters.title: Interception Attempt
chapters.summary: Vask's POV. Vask's team tries a rendezvous disguised as a rescue patrol; Mara spots the deception from a ridge. Shots fired into scree, no casualties, but now everyone knows they're hunted. Beat: open war declared on the mountain.

chapters.title: Renny's Fever
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Renny's wrist infects; Ilse, revealed to have medical training she hid to avoid attention, treats him. Her cover story cracks; she confesses she fled her father, not vacationed from him. Beat: vulnerability exchanged, crew cohesion deepening.

chapters.title: The Storm Wall
chapters.summary: August's POV. A multi-day storm pins them in a bivouac cave. Rations calculated, tempers frayed. August tells the full story of the disaster at last—including that Vask ordered the summit push that killed the climbers. Beat: confession as catharsis; hatred given a face.

chapters.title: White Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Storm-bound introspection; Mara admits she signed on because August's disgrace ruined her own career by association. Forgiveness offered, half-accepted. Beat: the cave as confessional; bonds forged in confinement.

chapters.title: Dev Makes His Choice
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Vask's beacon orders Dev to lead the party into an avalanche chute. Instead Dev destroys the beacon and confesses everything to August. Beat: redemption chosen at cost—now Dev is a marked man too.

chapters.title: The Chute Anyway
chapters.summary: August's POV. Weather forces them through the very chute Vask wanted; knowing the trap, August picks a marginal line. It holds—barely. One pack horse lost with half the food. Beat: terror and relief; the margin for error gone.

chapters.title: Hunger Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Renny's POV. Recalculated rations mean four days of half-meals. Renny, injured and slowing the group, offers to stay behind at a shelter hut. August refuses. Beat: the price of survival made literal; loyalty versus arithmetic.

chapters.title: Vask Closes the Valley
chapters.summary: Vask's POV. Vask's men occupy the lower exit hut and cut the safe descent. He radios August with an offer: hand over Ilse and the documents, walk away rich and unnamed. Beat: temptation framed precisely against August's history of following orders.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: August's POV. August's answer is one word. The crew debates—Tomas's voice in his memory, the ghosts of the dead climb. Ilse overhears and understands what his refusal costs him. Beat: character crystallized; point of no return.

chapters.title: Night Movement
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The crew moves at night along a glacier's edge to slip Vask's cordon. Near-catastrophe when a crevasse bridge collapses under Dev; rope work saves him. Beat: sustained suspense; teamwork as earned trust made physical.

chapters.title: The High Route
chapters.summary: August's POV. Only one path remains: the unclimbed shoulder August reconnoitered years ago and swore never to attempt. He lays out the risks honestly and lets each person choose. All six vote to go. Beat: agency reclaimed; fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Wind at the Shoulder
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The ascent proper: fixed lines, knife-edge traverses, Renny carried in shifts. Mara and August trade leads. Beat: the mountain rendered beautiful and indifferent; awe braided with exhaustion.

chapters.title: Ilse Above the Clouds
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. On a rest ledge above the cloud deck, Ilse decides she will not return to her father's world regardless of outcome. August, for the first time, speaks of a future tense. Beat: quiet love acknowledged without declaration.

chapters.title: Vask Climbs
chapters.summary: Vask's POV. Refused surrender, Vask commits his team to the same shoulder, gambling pride against sense. His men mutter; one deserts in the night. Beat: hubris accelerating; the antagonist mirroring the hero's route.

chapters.title: The Cornice
chapters.summary: August's POV. Near the crest, a cornice collapse sweeps Dev and a load of documents toward the void. Dev saves the satchel but shatters his leg on the anchor line. Beat: triumph inverted—victory purchased in blood.

chapters.title: Carrying Dev
chapters.summary: Renny's POV. The crew improvises a litter from tent poles and rope. Every hour of carrying costs daylight and heat. Renny, once willing to be left behind, now carries hardest. Beat: the theme embodied—survival is collective or nothing.

chapters.title: Summit Ridge, Last Light
chapters.summary: August's POV. They crest at dusk into brutal cold, the far valley visible below, descent impossible in darkness. They dig in on the ridge. Beat: exaltation shadowed by peril; the top of the world as the worst place to spend a night.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Multiple short POV turns (Ilse, Mara, Dev). Huddled survival through minus-thirty wind; stories told to stay awake; Dev fading. Beat: endurance as communion; the novel's emotional core—what people owe each other.

chapters.title: Dawn and Descent
chapters.summary: August's POV. Clear dawn, Dev alive but critical. A controlled glissade and down-climb consume the day. Vask's team is spotted far below, moving slower, breaking apart. Beat: grim momentum; the race inverted—now they descend while rivals fail.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Moraine
chapters.summary: Vask's POV. Vask intercepts them alone—his men gone—at the terminal moraine. He demands the documents at gunpoint; Ilse steps between them and names what he did on the old expedition. August talks him down from the trigger; Vask breaks. Beat: climax of wills, resolved without a killing blow.

chapters.title: The Valley Floor
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. They reach the ranger station at the valley mouth; a helicopter takes Dev. Ilse hands the documents to waiting investigators she contacted via the station radio. Vask, hollow, does not resist arrest. Beat: release; the truth delivered at last.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: August's POV. Weeks later, August testifies publicly, ending his invisibility by choice. The blacklist becomes irrelevant beside the record; the old expedition's blame is formally reassigned. Beat: identity reclaimed—being seen as the reward, not the punishment.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Recovery interlude: Renny's healed hand, Dev's new prosthetic and honest employment offer, Mara and August rebuilding their outfitting business. Not everything is repaired—two porters quit, and Tomas's memory weighs still. Beat: bittersweet accounting.

chapters.title: Henrik Brandt's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse faces her father across a lawyer's table, neither reconciled nor cruel. She declines his settlement and funds the rangers' rescue post instead. Beat: closure without absolution; power renounced rather than seized.

chapters.title: The Upper Fly in Spring
chapters.summary: August's POV, closing frame. A year later, August leads a small, honest trek up the lower Fly, Ilse beside him as a licensed guide-in-training. At Kettle Ford he pauses where the near-drowning happened and simply walks on. Final beat: the wilderness forgives nothing—but people can begin again.
